title: Padrón: separate the national rule from the local process
intro: The national rule is simple: register in the municipality where you normally live. The actual filing is municipal, so your town hall controls the appointment channel, local form and address evidence it asks you to provide.

items.label: Procedure
items.text: Alta or inscripción in the Padrón Municipal de Habitantes for the address where you normally live.

items.label: Where to go
items.text: Your own ayuntamiento (town hall). There is no single national padrón office or national appointment portal for this filing.

items.label: What to look for
items.text: On the town hall website, look for Padrón, Empadronamiento, Alta en el padrón or a similarly named municipal population-register service. The exact wording and whether you need an appointment vary by municipality.

items.label: Check locally before you go
items.text: Confirm the municipality's current form, appointment method and accepted proof of address. Do not copy another town's document list.

items.label: Usually prepare
bullets: Valid passport or national identity document
The address evidence your municipality accepts for your housing situation
Rental contract or property evidence where applicable
Authorisation or additional occupant/owner documents if your municipality requires them
Appointment confirmation if the local system requires an appointment

items.label: Ask for next
items.text: Ask how to obtain a volante or certificado de empadronamiento if another procedure needs proof. Padrón proves municipal residence/address; it does not itself grant immigration residence status.
